data.name: Puzzles Under The Hill
data.detailed_description:
Puzzles Under The Hill features Pamela Possum taking a stroll to visit her best friend Sammy Squirrel. Along the way, Pamela collects shiny jewels unveiling wonderful jigsaw challenges, featuring beautiful imagery from the National Gallery of Art. Your task is to join the adventure through the forest, passing sweet little cottages, putting together increasingly complex jigsaw puzzles. To complete the quest, each puzzle must be completed, and only by reaching the end will the two friends come together.

Key Features:

  • Solve jigsaw puzzles of varying complexity
  • 40 images from the National Gallery of Art
  • Cute, cherry, and beautiful 3D graphics
  • Fun, casual gameplay for everyone!

reviews.review:
If you viewed the screenshots, saw the backside of the cartoon opossum, the cute 3D version of Hobbitton, and a few yellow gems floating over the ground, you could be forgiven for thinking that you would control the possum, walk around, maybe jump on platforms, and that collecting gems would be part of the game.  But you would be wrong, because this game is from publisher Ensenasoft who, though they may have the best of the intentions, apparently have a game-development budget defined as "whatever we could find under the couch cushions."

Much like Ensenasoft's other title [url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/498040/]The Hidden Dragon[/url], [i]Puzzles Under The Hill[/i] is a game that doesn't know who its audience is.  The cute cartoon opossum, the periodic inane verse, the slow pace, the cutely saccharine story line, the fact that the puzzles all have helpful lines showing the layout of pieces so that you don't even need the image to solve it, and the fact that the very hardest puzzles cap out shy of a hundred pieces that don't even need to be rotated all suggest that this game was made for children.  But the puzzles you solve are all of Impressionist paintings, and the whole game is set to a lovely meditative soundtrack of classical guitar.  Children, as a demographic, are not notable for their appreciation of either Impressionism or classical guitar.

So, assuming that you're an adult player, you start the game up, quickly click through the doggerel verse explaining what the opossum is up to, try to take control, and discover that you're just along for the ride.  You can do nothing while Pamela Possum waddles her way to the first gem.  Once she gets it, you play a very easy jigsaw puzzle.  Since the first puzzle is easiest, you should have it completed in under thirty seconds.  It may be insultingly easy, in fact, but you can't skip ahead to the harder puzzles; you must do each in order, just like in their even worse game [url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/489890/]Puzzles at Mystery Manor[/url].  And between each puzzle, you must watch a cartoon possum's wiggling buttocks for a few seconds as she waddles through pseudo-Hobbitton, which will be of interest to no-one save the occasional furry.

That's the entire game apart from one twist: [spoiler]the friend you've gone to visit has gone fishing, so you have to walk the entire course again in the evening, allowing the game to get double-duty from its limited environment.[/spoiler]  Images and soundtrack aimed at adults, difficulty level and between-level segments strictly for kids, resulting in a game that that's pleasant for nobody.

I would totally buy the soundtrack, though.
